_note: Every number here is a design parameter with its origin in `source`. Prices are illustrative order-of-magnitude figures, not quotations; currents and seconds are typical datasheet or published values, not measurements made for this handbook. Replace them with your parts' datasheets and a measured connect sequence.
usable_battery_fraction_source: self-discharge, cold and cutoff voltage: a common derating for alkaline and Li-ion packs; measured packs decide

links.name: Wi-Fi + MQTT over TLS
links.range_source: 2.4 GHz to a domestic router across a yard, no walls in the way: tens of metres; a site survey decides
links.downlink_source: a subscribed MQTT client on a kept TLS session hears a publish within the broker round trip
links.per_device_source: the farm's existing internet; nothing per node

energy.sleep_source: ESP32 deep sleep is ~10 uA; a module with its regulator and a sensor ~50 uA (assumed)
energy.wake_source: association + DHCP + NTP + TLS session resumption + one publish, 3 s typical on an ESP32; 120 mA is a rough average of its Wi-Fi RX/TX currents (Espressif datasheet gives ~100 mA RX, up to 240 mA TX peaks)

links.name: LoRaWAN (EU868 plan) through a gateway
links.range_source: rural, antenna a few metres up, some trees: 2 km is conservative for SF7-SF9; 10 km+ needs line of sight and higher SF
links.max_payload_source: LoRaWAN Regional Parameters, EU863-870 maximum application payload (N) per data rate
links.airtime_budget_source: The Things Network Fair Use Policy: 30 s of uplink airtime per device per day on the community network. The regulatory 1 % duty cycle (36 s per hour per sub-band) is the only limit on a network server you run yourself; `airtime` prints both.
links.downlink_source: class C (receiver always on, mains only): a downlink within seconds. A class A node hears a downlink only in the two receive windows after its own uplink, so its latency is its uplink period; `select` applies that to battery nodes.
links.per_device_source: community network server free under fair use, or a self-hosted ChirpStack counted in chapter 8
links.site_source: one indoor 8-channel gateway, order of magnitude; shared by the plot and pump-house nodes (illustrative)

energy.sleep_source: MCU deep sleep + radio sleep (~1 uA) + sensor off (assumed)
energy.wake_source: wake, read the sensors, pack the frame (assumed)
energy.tx_source: +14 dBm on an SX1276-class radio: datasheet ~29 mA at +13 dBm, more on the PA_BOOST pin; 45 mA is a conservative round number
energy.rx_source: the two class A receive windows, mostly empty (assumed)

links.name: LTE-M / NB-IoT + MQTT over TLS
links.range_source: wherever the operator has coverage; the node's `cellular_coverage` flag
links.downlink_source: a registered modem with a kept session: seconds. A node in power-saving mode (PSM) is unreachable until its next wake, so a battery node's latency is its uplink period.
links.per_device_source: an IoT SIM with a few MB a month: the order of magnitude of published plans, not a quotation

energy.sleep_source: modem in PSM plus MCU deep sleep (assumed)
energy.wake_source: leave PSM, tracking-area update, TLS resumption, one publish: 2-10 s and 100-200 mA in published measurements; 5 s at 100 mA is a middle value (assumed)
